note: All frames are client-supplied photography of MayaQuad, Imi Ouaddar, collected by hand into intake/mayaquad/photos/ and processed to the layout's reserved ratios. No stock, no AI generation. `source` is the original filename in that directory.
cropping: Two-stage. Stage 1 is an explicit `extract` of a hand-measured branding-free `safe` box; stage 2 is a sharp `attention` crop to the target ratio inside it. Attention gravity ALONE is unsafe on this set — every usable frame carries a high-contrast blue MAYAQUAD logo block, and most sit inside a marketing graphic with a URL bar, which is exactly what an entropy heuristic locks onto. `safe` below is the stage-1 region in original-image pixels.
substitutions: Two slots have no literal subject in the client set and are filled with the truest available stand-in rather than left blank. fleet-scooter has no scooter, so it carries the destination (the Taghazout road sign) that its copy actually sells. fleet-moto has no clean motorbike frame — imgi_108_caption proves they run an orange enduro, but the MAYAQUAD watermark sits dead centre over it and cannot be cropped out — so it carries the country the tour crosses. A motorbike frame and a true headlights-in-the-dark night frame are the two shots still worth requesting.
recuration: Second pass over an enlarged folder (139 files, but only 6 genuinely new photographs; the rest is scraped browser chrome — Material icons, favicons, Google Maps sprites). Only one binding changed: night. Everything else was re-checked against its brief and kept, since a newer file is not by itself a better fit.
enhancement: These three are the weakest sources in the set, so each gets a tone pass (sharp `modulate` + `linear`) and an unsharp mask; fleet-moto and night are additionally upscaled with lanczos3. Tone and sharpening only — nothing that changes what the photograph shows. The site then applies its unified film grade over the top via the `.photo-film` utility.
excluded: Two frames in the intake are screenshots of the client's Google reviews. They are deliberately unused: that is third-party copyrighted text, and the same reason the page paraphrases review sentiment rather than quoting it.
